_comment: Version 3: every variant links OpenSSL, PCRE2 and zlib from their side campaigns' installs of the same variant (../<source>-bindings/crustify/builds/<variant>/install), through OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR and CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH; libc stays the system's. Version 4: the coverage variant compiles with clang 23's source-based coverage (-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping). Version 5: libgit2 builds with -fvisibility=hidden, so libgit2.so exports only its GIT_EXTERN API; the last step of every variant's build, crustify/scripts/static-archive.sh, archives the objects libgit2.so links (its own TUs and the deps/ object libraries it bundles, as build.ninja's link edge lists them) into the variant's `static`, crustify/libgit2.a, which campaign mode links statically so that the Rust reaches libgit2's internal functions; the C tests and the CLI still link libgit2.so. Version 6: the static archive is crustify/libcrustify.a, and holds every link unit's objects, the CLI's (git2) beside libgit2's. Version 7: src/util/utf8.c, the first module switched from C, has left c/, and the C that remains, libgit2.so, the CLI and the C tests, links the safe crate's Rust static library, each variant's `rust`, which its configure names to the fork's CMake (-DLIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY) and the first step of its build makes (crustify/scripts/rust-staticlib.sh): the crate of the checkout CRUSTIFY_ROOT names, built as a staticlib on the dev profile in campaign mode against the configured variant, linking none of its C, and instrumented as cargo-variant.sh instruments the variant's Rust. libgit2.so keeps the Rust's symbols local (--exclude-libs), and campaign mode leaves the library out of the Rust's own links. The variants are built in generations (crustify/scripts/build-variants.sh <generation dir>), a checkout's crustify/builds linking to one, each configured from the generation's own c, a worktree of the fork at the commit it was built from, so that a generation outlives the checkouts and C revisions after it: crustify/builds.gen1 is the first.
